_note: Placeholder practice challenges. General practice advice only, not official rules or judging criteria. Replace freely; the app validates this file on load.

challenges.title: Twelve identical shortbread fingers
challenges.summary: A short, low-stakes bake about consistency rather than flair.
challenges.goal: Twelve fingers the same size and thickness, evenly pale gold, all from one batch.
prepNotes: Weigh everything before you start the clock.
Decide how you'll make them the same size: a ruler, a template, or rolling guides.
Chilled dough holds its shape better, so plan a short rest in the fridge.
safetyNotes: Trays come out hot. Have a clear spot ready before you open the oven.
reflectionHints: How close were the sizes, honestly?
Was the colour even across the tray?

challenges.title: Six matching decorated cupcakes
challenges.summary: Bake, cool and finish six cupcakes that look like a set.
challenges.goal: Six cupcakes with level tops and the same piped finish, presented together.
prepNotes: Cooling takes longer than you think. Work out when they must leave the oven.
Practise one swirl on a plate before the first cupcake.
Pick the plate or board you'll present on before you begin.
safetyNotes: Let cakes cool fully before decorating, and keep anything with fresh cream cold.
reflectionHints: Did they look like a set from arm's length?
Where did the time actually go?

challenges.title: A Swiss roll without cracks
challenges.summary: A whisked sponge, a filling and a clean roll.
challenges.goal: An even spiral, no cracks on the outside, cleanly trimmed ends.
prepNotes: Line the tin before you whisk anything.
Have your rolling paper and filling ready for the moment the sponge comes out.
Decide whether you'll roll warm or cool, and stick with it.
safetyNotes: Rolling a hot sponge means handling something straight from the oven. Use a clean tea towel or paper, not bare hands.
reflectionHints: Was the sponge too thick, too dry, or just right?
Did the filling spread evenly to the edges?

challenges.title: A fruit tart in two hours
challenges.summary: Shortcrust, blind baking, crème pâtissière and a neat finish.
challenges.goal: A crisp, evenly baked case, a set filling and fruit arranged with intent.
prepNotes: Write down the order: pastry, chill, blind bake, crème pât, cool, assemble.
Crème pât needs time to cool. Make it while the pastry chills.
Plan the fruit pattern on paper before you cut anything.
safetyNotes: Hot baking beans hold heat for a long time. Tip them somewhere safe to cool.
Custard fillings should be cooled quickly and kept in the fridge.
reflectionHints: Was the base crisp all the way to the centre?
Which step ran over, and why?

challenges.title: Éclairs against the clock
challenges.summary: Choux pastry, piping and a glossy finish under time pressure.
challenges.goal: Twelve éclairs of matching length, crisp and hollow, filled and glazed.
prepNotes: Mark piping guides on your paper before you start.
Choux needs to dry out properly. Build that into your timings.
Have the filling chilling while the shells bake.
safetyNotes: The panade is very hot when you beat in the eggs. Let it cool slightly first.
reflectionHints: Did any collapse? When in the bake did it happen?
How consistent was the piping from first to last?

challenges.title: A plaited loaf in three hours
challenges.summary: An enriched dough, two proves and a plait that holds its shape.
challenges.goal: An even, well-risen plait with a deep, glossy crust and a fully baked middle.
prepNotes: Proving is the bit you can't rush. Work backwards from when it must go in the oven.
Practise the plait with string or tea towels first if it's new to you.
Find the warmest draught-free spot in your kitchen before you start.
safetyNotes: Check the bake by tapping the base or with a thermometer, using oven gloves.
reflectionHints: Was it under- or over-proved? What told you?
Did the plait stay even along its length?
